instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you serve.
Meanwhile, slice the cucumbers into rounds and set them on a plate. Squeeze 2 tsp of lime juice into a large bowl and cut the rest of the lime into wedges.
Crack the eggs into the bowl with the lime juice. Add 4 tsp tamari and sprinkle in 4 tsp cornstarch. Whisk with a fork for 1 minute, until there are no lumps and no streaks of white.
Pour the oil into an 8 inch skillet. It should be about 1/4 inch deep. Heat it over medium-high for 3 minutes, until a drop of the egg sizzles the moment it lands.
Stand back a little. It will spatter. Pour in a quarter of the eggs. They'll puff and bubble right away. Cook for 1 minute, until the underside is deep golden and the edges are crisp.
Flip it and cook the other side for 30 seconds. Transfer it to a plate lined with paper towels.
Taste a corner of the first omelette. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt to the eggs that are left.
Make 3 more omelettes the same way, whisking the eggs before each pour.
Serve the omelettes over the rice with the cucumber, the lime wedges and the sriracha on the side.
method_notes: Every source agrees on the core: beaten eggs with fish sauce, poured into a lot of very hot oil so the omelette puffs and goes crisp at the edges. Some add cornstarch or rice flour for extra crunch (Saveur-style) and some add lime juice. The sources use fish sauce; this uses tamari so it stays vegetarian and gluten-free. No source had 20 or more ratings, and the lead is the best-rated one that could be read.
